source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: What lesson does the seat-minder build illustrate about directing an agent to write software, according to the notes?

options.text: Moving the typing to an agent does not remove the need to state requirements
options.feedback: Correctness, concurrency, and privacy still have to be asked for out loud. The seat-minder concurrency risk is the same category of bug a hand-written system would have to guard against.

options.text: An agent finds and fixes every bug in a build without being asked to
options.feedback: The notes show the opposite: defensive, non-blocking code had to be requested explicitly rather than turning up unprompted.

options.text: Agents can only build software that has no database behind it at all
options.feedback: Seat-minder runs on a Postgres-compatible database, so the notes contradict this one directly.

options.text: Directing an agent removes the need for a clear problem statement first
options.feedback: The sequence runs the other way: the North Star problem statement came first, and the agent-directed build followed from it.
